2. The petitioner stated, inter cilia, that he is a business man by profession and started, the business under the name and style "Foto Fast Color Lab" in the year 1992 after obtaining necessary Certificate from the Dhaka Municipal Corporation on 21-7-1991 and opened a letter of credit for import of the machine in 1991 and upon arrival of the machineries submitted bill of entry together with all relevant papers, for delivery of the machineries for the business in the month of June, 1992. The petitioner obtained sanction from the authority of 440 power line for starting business and god itself registered with the VAT authority on 21-1-1992 as required under section 15 of the VAT Act 1991 but after installation of the machinery the project of Photo Processing and printing was started on 1-7-1992, Since starting the petitioner has been maintaining proper and regular accounts of daily output and sale proceeds in a Tax assessment book as required under Rule 22(1) of the VAT Rules and on being satisfied by the Inspector customs, Excise and VAT about the quantity of production, sale proceeds and the amount, of VAT imposed by the Inspector and the petitioner has been paying the actual amount of VAT by depositing Challan which were duly endorsed by the said Inspector till date. Accordingly the petitioner paid Taka 20,362.00 as VAT for the period 11 months starting from July 1992 month to Month basis as determined and approved by the customs and VAT authority. While the petitioner was carrying on the business payment of regular VAT duly endorsed by its Inspector the petitioner to his utter surprise received a notice dated 5-7-1993 issued by the Assistant Collector (now designated as Assistant Commissioner) stating that on the basis of the report from the concerned Circle the monthly average VAT was at Taka 19,877/81 and as such the petitioner was asked to pay Taka 1,98,316.(X) after depleting the amount of Taka 2(1.340.00 already paid for the period from July, 1991 to May, 1993; The petitioner has further asserted that he as neither given copy of the alleged report nor the petitioner received any objection against the monthly payment of VAT. The petitioner filed an objection thereto stating payment of actual and correct amount of VAT duly endorsed by the concerned inspector and there was no area whatsoever, and as such there could not be any notice tier any arrear as alleged. The petitioner further asserted that he has not received, objection on the question of amount of VAT and no enquiry was held within the knowledge of the petitioner and requested the respondent no 5 to withdraw the illegal demand which was violative of the principle of natural justice. The petitioner was asked to appear before the respondent No- 5 on 20-7-1993 for hearing which upon several adjournment ultimately was heard on 21-8-1993 on which date the petitioner was on 21-8-1993 on which date the petitioner was heard and in support of his submitted relevant papers justifying the amount of VAT already paid which has been duly endorsed and authenticated by the inspector of the circle. The petitioner has further asserted that there is no calculation of VAT on monthly average as the business of film processing and printing varies from day to day and season to season inasmuch as the business is almost a seasonal one, and as such the calculation of the amount of Vat on average basis has been done without any factual foundation and contrary to provision of law inasmuch as the respondent has illegally and arbitrarily determined the output of the petitioner. Whereas the petitioner after installation of the machinery and from starting the business 1st July, 1992 and since then having been paying the VAT regularly for the concerned period with due endorsement in the register by the Inspector who as well passed the challan for payment of VAT. The petitioner preferred an appeal under section 42 of the VAT Act which, however, was dismissed by the Commissioner, respondent No. 4 without discussing and considering the case of the petitioner on merit on 16-9-1996 as being barred by limitation and further appeal before the Appellate Tribunal was also dismissed without considering the case on merit on the ground of barred by limitation by order dated 2-6-1997. Thus the petitioner being aggrieved has moved this court thereafter and obtained the present Rule and stay. 

 3. At the time of hearing of the Rule the petitioner by way of supplementary affidavit further asserted that since the receipt of demand notice dated 5-7-1993 the petitioner had been unsuccessfully crying that no show cause notice or any enquiry whatsoever was held in respect of past and closed transaction and that the petitioner`s appeal was rejecter on the flimsy ground of being barred by limitation instead of considering the grievance of the petitioner and not being served with any show cause notice or not holding any enquiry as contemplated under section 45 of the VAT Act, 1991 prior to re-opening of the alleged suppressed assessment of VAT whereas the petitioner although has been challenging the legality and propriety of the notice of demand as arbitrary and fictitious demand notice dated 5-7-93 and prayer for re-hearing upon issuing the show cause notice and appropriate enquiry in the matter. 

 4. Mr Rafiqul Islam the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner has taken us through the Annexures particularly Annexure-A the Trade licence issued Dhaka municipal Corporation, Annexure-B the enrollment with the VAT authority dated 21-1-1992 and Annexure C (series) showing actual commencement of business by installing machinery with effect from July 1992 duly certified and endorsed by Inspector Customs Excise and VAT, Ramna Circle, Dhaka and has submitted that the petitioner upon commencement of business with effect from 1st July, 1992 having been assessed with VAT on the day to day income of the petitioner as per register maintained for the purpose and pair the VAT on the basis of challan duly passed by the Inspector of the area, the abrupt sudden issuance of demand notice dated 5-7-1993 issued by the Assistant Commissioner of the circle with arbitrary and fictitious demand a total amount of Taka 1,98,361.00 for a period from July, 1911 to May, 1993 on imaginary amount of average monthly VAT at Taka 19,87780 has been done not o0nly without any factual basis but also without any show cause notice for the purpose of re-opening the assessment and holding any enquiry whatsoever in violation of the principle of natural justice also the provision of section 47 of the VAT Act and as such the alleged dismissal of appeal solely on the ground of the same being barred by limitation have been done without any lawful authority inasmuch as the ends of justice warrant that prior to any such re-opening a show cause notice for any such demand dated 5-7-1993. The authority was obliged to issue a show cause notice and enquiry. The learned Counsel has further submitted that in view of the Annexure-C (series) the payment of regular VAT on monthly basis duly inspected and authenticated and endorsed by the Inspector, the arbitrary re-opening of the issue and that demand for a fictitious amount of Taka 1,98,316.00 on the basis of an imaginary monthly average an amount of Taka 19,877/81 has been done illegally and the same having no basis whatsoever either in law of in fact has rendered the same to be declared without any lawful authority. The notice of this Rule have been duly served upon the respondents but they did not contest the Rule by filing affidavit-in-opposition but at the time of hearing the learned Deputy Attorney General Mr Obaidur Rahman Mostafa has appeared in the matter and made his submission supporting the impugned order and has submitted that the petitioner could agitate his grievance before the appellate authority on filing the appeal in timer and as such could not be allowed to re-open the thing which has been fought unsuccessfully up to the appellate stage. 

 5. The petitioner has asserted that he has obtained a licence from the Dhaka Municipal Corporation for starting the business of photo processing and printing on 21-7-1991, thereafter the petitioner has opened letter off-Credit for importing the machinery and accessories towards the end of the year 1991 and upon arrival of the same submitted, bill of entry together with all relevant papers for delivery and got the delivery of the machinery sometime in May/June, 1992, Thereafter the petitioner by installing of 440 Volt power line required for the business obtained the necessary permission from the authority and commenced business with effect from 1st July, 1992. It Appears from Annexure-C' which is a register maintaining account from the month of July, 1992 onwards with endorsement by Inspector, Customs, VAT, Ramna. Circle-Dhaka and issuing Challan for depositing the, VAT on month basis while the petitioner as well on 21-1-1992 with itself registered with the VAT authority, The petitioner has asserted that as per business and his endorsement on the register duly inspected and authenticated by the Inspector VAT authority, the petitioner has already paid tax on month basis an amount of Taka 20,362.00 for the concerned period but inspite of that all on a sudden without any show cause notice and without any enquiry the impugned order of demand dated 5-7-93 was issued by the Assistant Collector (now designated as Assistant Commissioner) demanding total amount of Taka 1,98,316.00 on the basis of a monthly average of Taka 19,877.81 without giving the petitioner a copy of the alleged report of the concerned Circle. It appears from Annexure "E" dated 11-7-1993 that the petitioner has categorically stated that there was no arrear of VAT and as such no such demand notice dated 5-7-1993 is applicable to the petitioner. The petitioner has further asserted that the same was issued without even any prior notice to the petitioner. By subsequent representation in Annexure-'G' the petitioner by way of an appeal has asserted that there was no an-ear due and that the petitioner has but been served with any notice or any enquiry was held so as to re-open the past and closed transaction as to payment of VAT but the Commissioner by its order dated 16-9-1996 without considering on merit in accordance with law and the issue involved therein rejected the appeal on the ground of limitation. Thereafter the petitioner by way of representation preferred an appeal, to the appellate authority on 21-12-1996 but the same way as well dismissed on 2-6-1997 without considering the issues involved therein on the ground of being barred by limitation. Thereafter another demand notice was issued which has been impugned before us. Meanwhile, it appears from Annexure-E (Series) that the petitioner was issued with notice of hearing of the objection of the petitioner dated 11-7-1993 allegedly before the Assistant Commissioner...but without any formal order discussing the issues involved in the matter, the Superintendent, Customs Excise and VAT respondent No. 6. by its demand notice dated 5-6-1996 i.e. after lapse of about 2 years 10 months has issued another demand notice claiming an amount of Taka 1,98,316.00 on the account of VAT. It appears from the impugned order dated 2-6-1997 that the petitioner was heard on 214-1993 pursuant to the said notice Annexure-E (2) but no order was passed on merit upon hearing the petitioner, instead a further notice reiterating the claim in notice dated 5-7-1993 was issued on 22-8-93 asking the petitioner to pay the amount by 30-8-1993. The petitioner has asserted that he has not only been served with the said notice by the Assistant Commissioner but has also not received the said notice and after about 2 years 10 months the notice dated 5-6-1996 was issued for which the petitioner could not prefer the alleged appeal in time. 

 6. It further appears from the impugned order dated 14-10-1996 of the Commissioner's (Appeal) while dismissing the appeal as barred by limitation has illegally construed the alleged demand but as a matter of fact on perusal of the same in Annexure-D1 it is very much clear that on the fact of the matter the same was a demand simpliciter claiming Taka 1,98,316.00 due from the petitioner for alleged government revenue.
